AmountOrScalar.description:
Value that can be currency-aware or unitless.

Used for node values that can represent:
- **Amount**: Currency-aware monetary values (e.g., USD 1,000,000)
- **Scalar**: Unitless values (e.g., ratios, percentages, counts)

BalanceSheetArticulation.description:
Verifies that Assets = Liabilities + Equity at every model period close.

Each group names known nodes, with no identifier repeated within a group
or shared between groups: the caller includes each account once, through
its subtotal or its components. All operands have compatible units and
one currency; the check performs no FX conversion. Signed balances and
typed zeros are used as they are.

Monetary balances are summed exactly and scalar balances with compensated
sums. The signed difference is `assets - (liabilities + equity)`; the
relative reference of the tolerance is `|assets|`. A period with a
missing balance is incomplete and names the nodes without a value; the
check passes only when every period is complete and within tolerance.

assets_nodes.description: Node IDs whose values represent total assets.

equity_nodes.description: Node IDs whose values represent total equity.

liabilities_nodes.description: Node IDs whose values represent total liabilities.

tolerance.description:
Absolute tolerance override in the balances' units; replaces both
terms of the suite's
[`CheckConfig`](crate::checks::CheckConfig) allowance.

BuiltinCheckSpec.description:
Tagged enum describing any built-in check in a serializable form.

Each variant wraps its check struct, so the struct is the single schema;
the JSON shape is the struct's fields plus a `type` tag. Convert into a
boxed [`Check`] via [`BuiltinCheckSpec::to_check`].

oneOf.description: Balance sheet articulation: Assets = Liabilities + Equity.
Cash balance reconciliation: Cash(t) = Cash(t-1) + TotalCF(t).
Flags required nodes that lack values in applicable periods.

CashReconciliation.description:
Reconciles closing cash to opening cash plus classified cash flows and
separately identified adjustments, and independently reconciles total
classified cash flows to CFO + CFI + CFF.

The roll-forward is evaluated for every model period:
`closing = opening + total cash flow + adjustments`. The first opening is
the explicit `opening_balance` at the first period boundary; each later
opening is the close of the immediately adjacent prior period. Cash
inflows are positive and outflows negative. All inputs share one cash
scope, compatible units and one currency; the check performs no FX
conversion.

The component identity `total cash flow = CFO + CFI + CFF` runs for every
period when all three component nodes are configured, and not at all when
none is; configuring only some of them is an error.

Monetary comparisons are exact and scalar ones compensated. The relative
reference of the tolerance is `|opening cash|` for the roll-forward and
`|total cash flow|` for the components, with no floor. A comparison with
a missing input is incomplete; the check passes only when every enabled
comparison is complete and within tolerance.

adjustment_nodes.description: Signed FX and cash-scope adjustment nodes, each included once.

cash_balance_node.description: Node for the closing cash balance of each period.

cfo_node.description:
Node for cash from operations; configure all three components or
none.

opening_balance.description: Opening cash at the start of the model's first period.

tolerance.description:
Absolute tolerance override in the cash units; replaces both terms of
the suite's [`CheckConfig`](crate::checks::CheckConfig) allowance.

total_cash_flow_node.description: Node for total classified cash flow of each period, inflows positive.

CheckCategory.description: Category that groups related checks together.

oneOf.description: Balance sheet balances, retained earnings flow-through, cash ties
Depreciation ties to PP&E, interest ties to debt schedule, etc.
Growth rate plausibility, effective tax rate range, WC consistency
Leverage ranges, coverage floors, FCF sign, liquidity runway

CheckConfig.description:
Configuration parameters that govern check execution.

The identity tolerance is zero unless one is stated: an identity then
holds only when its two sides are equal. An explicit tolerance allows
`|difference| <= max(default_tolerance, default_relative_tolerance *
|reference|)`, where the reference is the identity owner's (total assets
for the balance sheet, for example); a difference equal to the allowance
is within tolerance. A per-check absolute override replaces both terms.

`materiality_threshold` and `min_severity` are reporting filters for
advisory findings. They never change a verdict, and they never remove an
error-severity finding, a coverage finding or a recorded comparison.

default_relative_tolerance.description:
**Relative** tolerance as a fraction of the identity's reference
value (1e-9 allows 10 on a reference of 1e10). Zero, the default,
disables the relative term.

default_tolerance.description:
**Absolute** tolerance for equality comparisons, in the units of the
compared values (0.01 is one cent when nodes are in whole dollars).
Zero, the default, requires exact equality.

materiality_threshold.description:
Advisory findings whose absolute materiality is below this threshold
are left out of the report. Error-severity and coverage findings are
always reported.

min_severity.description:
Minimum severity an advisory finding must have to appear in the
report. Coverage findings are always reported.

CheckSeverity.description: Severity level for a check finding, ordered from least to most severe.

oneOf.description: Error — indicates a likely problem that should be addressed.

CheckSuiteSpec.description:
Serializable descriptor for a [`CheckSuite`] that can be saved/loaded as
JSON for team-wide check policies.

Both built-in and formula checks are resolved by [`CheckSuiteSpec::resolve`].

DateWire.description: ISO 8601 calendar date encoded as a `YYYY-MM-DD` JSON string.

DatedOpening.description:
An explicit opening balance at the first period boundary of a
roll-forward identity.

date.description: Date of the balance: the start of the model's first period.

value.description:
The balance on that date, in the units and currency of the
reconciled balance node. A known zero is a typed zero.

DecimalWire.description:
Exact decimal encoded only as a JSON string.

Restoration routes through [`crate::decimal::parse_decimal`], the single
exact text-admission rule: JSON numbers, malformed text and inexact values
are rejected rather than rounded. Serialization writes canonical
fixed-point text with trailing zeros removed and signed zero normalized
(`"1.5"`, `"0"`), never scientific notation.

FormulaCheckSpec.description:
Serializable, runnable user-defined formula-check specification.

Full suite definitions (built-in + formula) can be stored as a single JSON
document and resolved directly with [`CheckSuiteSpec::resolve`].

Each period ends in one of three verdicts: pass, fail (a finding with the
configured `severity`), or insufficient data. A period has insufficient
data when a same-period input is missing or non-finite, or when the
formula consumes a non-finite value, such as a lag or rolling window that
reaches before the first period. It is reported as a `warning` finding
naming the inputs, records no comparison, and never fails the check. A
division by zero over finite inputs is not missing data and still fails.

formula.description:
Statements DSL expression to evaluate (e.g. `"revenue > 0"`).

Formula checks use the same evaluator as calculated statement nodes,
including time-series functions and `cs.*` capital-structure references.

id.description: Unique identifier for this check instance.

message_template.description: Template for the finding message (`{period}` is replaced at runtime).

severity.description: Severity assigned to findings when the formula fails.

tolerance.description:
Finite, nonnegative absolute residual bound in the formula's result units.
When present, the formula passes when its absolute result is at most
this bound. When absent, the formula is a predicate and any finite
nonzero result passes.

MissingValueCheck.description:
Flags required nodes that lack values in applicable periods.

Missing actual observations produce `Severity::Error` and fail the check.
Missing forecast observations produce advisory `Severity::Warning` findings.

required_nodes.description: Nodes that must have values in every in-scope period.

amount.description:
Monetary amount, carried on the wire as an exact decimal string rather
than a JSON number so no precision is lost in transit. Construction with
configuration applies the selected ingest scale; raw construction does not.

currency.description:
ISO 4217 currency of `amount`. Arithmetic between two `Money` values
requires this to match; there is no implicit conversion.

NonFiniteCheck.description:
Detects NaN or infinite values in node results.

**Gating**: findings are `Severity::Error`, so any non-finite cell sets
`CheckResult::passed` to `false` and fails a pipeline gate. Non-finite
values poison every downstream calculation, so they are never advisory.

nodes.description: Specific nodes to check; if empty, all nodes in results are inspected.

PeriodScope.description: Scope that determines which periods a check applies to.

oneOf.description: Run the check on every period.

RetainedEarningsReconciliation.description:
Reconciles retained earnings in every model period:
`closing = opening + net income + dividend effect + direct adjustments`.

The first opening is the explicit `opening_balance` at the first period
boundary; each later opening is the close of the immediately adjacent
prior period. All inputs share one ownership scope, compatible units and
one currency; the check performs no FX conversion.

# Sign convention

* `net_income_node` is signed: a profit increases retained earnings and
  a loss decreases it.
* `dividends_node` is, by default
  ([`SignConventionPolicy::MagnitudePositive`]), a non-negative magnitude
  that the identity subtracts; a negative magnitude is rejected. Under
  [`SignConventionPolicy::InflowPositive`] it is a signed amount the
  identity adds.
* `other_adjustments` are signed entries recorded directly in retained
  earnings, each a distinct node included once. A restatement appears
  once: in an already-restated opening balance or as one such entry.

Omit a dividend or adjustment series only when it does not apply; a
configured series without a value makes the period incomplete, and a
known zero is a typed zero. Monetary comparisons are exact and scalar
ones compensated. The relative reference of the tolerance is
`|opening retained earnings|`, with no floor. The check passes only when
every period is complete and within tolerance.

dividends_node.description: Node for dividends recognized in retained earnings in each period.

net_income_node.description: Node for net income of each period, signed.

opening_balance.description: Opening retained earnings at the start of the model's first period.

other_adjustments.description: Signed direct retained-earnings entries, each a distinct node.

retained_earnings_node.description: Node for the closing retained-earnings balance of each period.

tolerance.description:
Absolute tolerance override in the balance units; replaces both terms
of the suite's [`CheckConfig`](crate::checks::CheckConfig) allowance.

SignConventionCheck.description:
Flags values with unexpected signs (e.g., revenue < 0 or expense > 0).

**Advisory-only**: every finding is `Severity::Warning`, so this check's
`CheckResult::passed` is always `true` and it never fails a pipeline gate.
Treat its findings as review prompts, not assertions.

negative_nodes.description: Nodes expected to carry negative values.

positive_nodes.description: Nodes expected to carry positive values.

SignConventionPolicy.description:
Declared sign convention for a flow / magnitude input to a reconciliation
check.

Each reconciliation declares its input expectation so callers can
validate data at construction time rather than at P&L
reconciliation. Previously each reconciliation embedded its sign
assumptions implicitly (e.g. `CapexReconciliation` expected
`capex_cf` to be a positive magnitude while INVARIANTS.md §3
documented the CFS convention as negative), which produced silent
cross-check failures on any model that used the other convention.

# Variants

* [`Self::MagnitudePositive`] — the value is a non-negative magnitude;
  direction (inflow vs outflow) is encoded in the reconciliation's
  formula via `+` / `-` operators. Used by capex, depreciation,
  dividends, and disposal magnitudes across the cross-statement
  reconciliations.
* [`Self::InflowPositive`] — the value is a signed flow where positive
  means "inflow" / "addition" and negative means "outflow" /
  "reduction". Used by `total_cash_flow` in `CashReconciliation` and
  `net_income` in `RetainedEarningsReconciliation`.

oneOf.description:
The value must be a non-negative magnitude (the reconciliation's
formula adds or subtracts it explicitly). This is the default for
historical reasons — every reconciliation in the current code
assumes magnitudes are positive.

The value is signed: positive = inflow / addition, negative =
outflow / reduction.

TerminalValueSpec.description: Terminal value calculation method for DCF.

oneOf.description: Gordon Growth Model: TV = FCF_terminal × (1 + g) / (WACC - g)

stable_growth_rate.description:
Perpetual stable growth rate as an annual decimal (e.g., 0.02 for
2%). Must be < WACC.

oneOf.description:
H-Model: linear fade from high growth to stable growth (Damodaran).

```text
TV = FCF_T × (1+g_s)/(WACC-g_s) + FCF_T × H × (g_h-g_s)/(WACC-g_s)
```

where `H` is the half-life in years of the high-growth fade period.
The first term is the standard Gordon Growth stable-state value;
the second term captures the present value of excess growth that
linearly decays from `high_growth_rate` to `stable_growth_rate`
over `2 × half_life_years`.

half_life_years.description: Half-life of the growth fade in years (e.g., 5.0).

stable_growth_rate.description: Long-run stable growth rate (e.g., 0.03 for 3%). Must be < WACC.

description: Optional DCF, coverage, check-suite, valuation-date and LTV settings of the corporate analysis pipeline.

as_of.description:
Valuation date (ISO `YYYY-MM-DD`); required when a market context is
supplied.

cfads_node.description:
Statement node supplying cash flow available for debt service; `None`
leaves DSCR out of the credit metrics.

check_suite.description:
Check suite run against the statement evaluation. DCF and
capital-structure analyses require one that includes the `non_finite`
built-in check.

interest_coverage_node.description:
Statement node used as the interest-coverage numerator; `None` uses
`"ebitda"`.

ltv_value_node.description:
Statement node supplying a per-period LTV denominator; `None`
broadcasts a positive DCF enterprise value instead.

net_debt_override.description:
Flat net debt in model currency used instead of the model-derived
equity bridge; only read when `wacc` is set.

terminal_value.description:
Terminal-value method for the DCF; required when `wacc` is set and
ignored otherwise.

wacc.description:
Weighted average cost of capital as a decimal (`0.10` = 10%). Setting it
enables the DCF equity valuation and requires `terminal_value`.
